title: Onboarding
intro: Work top to bottom. Tick each step as you finish it - your progress is saved in this browser. Steps that produce a file or a set of resources link straight to the pill that generates it.

steps.title: Raise the onboarding request ticket
steps.detail: One ticket per product. The platform team picks it up within two working days.

instructions: Open your Jira project and pick the "Platform onboarding" request type.
Fill in the tenant and product names exactly as you will use them everywhere else.
Submit, and note the ticket key - the steps below reference it.
Install Atlassian's own CLI (acli), or ankitpokhrel/jira-cli if you prefer it.
Confirm the exact flags against your Jira version - the subcommand names have changed across releases (Jira now calls issues "work items").
Note the key it prints; the steps below reference it.

actions.label: the acli call
actions.command: acli jira workitem create --project PLAT --type Task --summary "Onboard <tenant>/<product>"

steps.title: Request write access to your product repository
steps.detail: You need this before any of the files below can be pushed.

instructions: Open the access portal and search for your product repository.
Request the Write role, naming the onboarding ticket as justification.
Wait for the approval mail before continuing.

steps.title: Bootstrap your local checkout
steps.detail: Installs the toolchain and runs the same checks CI does.

instructions: Run these from the repository root.

steps.title: Create your namespace and its RBAC
steps.detail: Rendered from your tenant and product on the Kubernetes pill - copy it and kubectl apply it.

instructions: Open the Kubernetes pill, fill in your tenant and product, and hit Copy all.
Paste the manifests into the command below and press Ctrl-D.
Switch to the Administrator perspective.
Go to Home -> Projects and click Create Project.
Name it <tenant>-<product>, matching the Kubernetes pill exactly.
Then go to User Management -> Roles to add the Role and RoleBinding.

steps.title: Commit config.yaml for your tenant
steps.detail: Fill it in on the Tenant Config tab, then push it with the link there.

instructions: Fill the form on the Tenant Config pill, copy the YAML, then commit it.

actions.command: git add config.yaml && git commit -m "feat: add tenant config" && git push

instructions: Fill the form on the Tenant Config pill until the YAML panel says Valid.
Hit Push to GitHub and follow the create-or-update link it reveals.
Commit on the branch GitHub opens for you.

actions.command: git add ci.yml && git commit -m "feat: add ci config" && git push

instructions: Fill the CI pill, then use its Push to GitHub link.

actions.command: git add cd.yml && git commit -m "feat: add cd config" && git push

instructions: Fill the CD pill, then use its Push to GitHub link.

steps.title: Verify the pipeline runs green end to end
steps.detail: Push a no-op commit and confirm build, test and deploy all pass.

instructions: Open the Actions tab on your repository and watch the latest run.
Then check your namespace in the console for the deployed workload.

steps.title: Ask your platform contact to sign the onboarding off
